The evidence in Source [S8], Source [S1], and Source [S13] explicitly shows the code `inds = torch.searchsorted(cdf, u, right=True)`. In Python's `torch.searchsorted` (and `numpy.searchsorted`), the `side='right'` argument means that if the value `u` is equal to an element in the sorted array `cdf`, the insertion point is placed after (to the right of) that element. Since the CDF represents cumulative probabilities where `cdf[i]` is the upper bound of bin `i-1` (or similar indexing depending on prepending zeros), placing the index to the right of the boundary value effectively assigns the sample to the bin starting at that boundary (the 'right' bin relative to the boundary point). Specifically, if `u == cdf[k]`, `searchsorted(..., right=True)` returns `k+1` (assuming 0-based indexing and standard behavior where it finds the first index where elements are greater than `u` for `left`, or greater than or equal for `right`? Actually, `right=True` returns the index after any existing entries of `u`. So if `cdf[k] == u`, it returns `k+1`. The logic in the code then uses `inds` to determine `below` and `above`. `below = inds - 1` and `above = inds`. If `inds = k+1`, then `below = k` and `above = k+1`. The bin is defined by `bins_g[..., 0]` (lower bound) and `bins_g[..., 1]` (upper bound). The CDF values gathered are `cdf_g[..., 0]` (CDF at `below`) and `cdf_g[..., 1]` (CDF at `above`). If `u` equals the upper boundary of bin `k` (which is `cdf[k+1]` in a standard setup where `cdf` has an extra zero at the start, or `cdf[k]` if no extra zero), the assignment to the 'right' bin (the next bin) is consistent with the `right=True` parameter's behavior of pushing the index to the right of the equality match. Thus, the evidence supports the claim.)
